services.name: Gusto
services.tagline: Online payroll with automatic federal, state and local tax filing, contractor payments and published prices for every plan
services.pricing_summary: From $49/mo + $6/person (Simple); Plus $80/mo + $12/person; Premium $180/mo + $22/person; Contractor Only $35/mo + $6/contractor for businesses with no W-2 employees ($0 base for the first 6 months as of 2026-09-30).
services.long_description:
Gusto is a payroll, benefits and HR company based in San Francisco. It was incorporated in 2011 as ZenPayroll, and its SEC Form D filings list ZenPayroll, Inc. and Switchboard Labs, Inc. as former names. Gusto is privately held. Gusto's pricing page says it is trusted by more than 500,000 businesses.

Gusto has been a buyer rather than a target. It completed its purchase of Guideline, a retirement plan provider, in 2025, and in April 2026 it announced the acquisition of Mosey, a business compliance platform. Gusto says Mosey's technology will become Gusto Business Compliance, covering state and local registrations, filings and renewals.

Gusto publishes prices for its main plans. Simple is $49/mo plus $6/mo per person and, per Gusto, is meant for businesses that run payroll in one state: full-service payroll, unlimited payroll runs, automatic federal, state and local tax filing, and basic PTO and holiday pay. Plus ($80/mo plus $12/person) adds multi-state payroll, faster pay timing, time tracking and more HR and benefits tools. Premium is $180/mo plus $22/person and adds dedicated support, HR guidance, and same-day and instant pay. A Contractor Only plan costs $35/mo plus $6/mo per contractor for businesses with no W-2 employees; as of 2026-09-30 Gusto discounts its base price to $0 for the first 6 months.

For trade shops, the connections that matter are accounting and field-service time tracking. Gusto syncs payroll to QuickBooks Online and Xero; on Xero, the sync can be split by employee, department, job title or Gusto project. Jobber's help center documents a Gusto integration that sends approved timesheet hours and reimbursable expenses from Jobber to Gusto on Jobber's Connect plan or higher, for hourly employees only. Housecall Pro lists Gusto on its integrations page.

The trade-off: Simple covers one state, so a shop with crews working across state lines needs Plus or above, and time tracking is a paid add-on on Simple. The per-person fee grows with the crew: 10 people cost $109/mo on Simple or $200/mo on Plus at list price.
services.how_it_works: Choose a plan on Gusto's website and add your company, bank and employee or contractor details. Each pay period you enter hours or bring them in from a connected time-tracking app, review the payroll and approve it; on its payroll plans Gusto files federal, state and local payroll taxes automatically. If you use Jobber, approved timesheet hours (and, optionally, reimbursable expenses) sync into an unprocessed Gusto payroll. If you use QuickBooks Online or Xero, each payroll run syncs to your books. Time tracking is included on Plus and Premium and is a paid add-on on Simple.

pros_detail.title: Published prices for every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Simple ($49/mo + $6/person), Plus ($80/mo + $12/person), Premium ($180/mo + $22/person) and Contractor Only ($35/mo + $6/contractor) are listed on Gusto's pricing page, so you can price it before talking to anyone.

pros_detail.title: Automatic tax filing from the entry plan
pros_detail.explanation: Gusto says Simple includes full-service payroll, unlimited payroll runs and automatic federal, state and local tax filing.

pros_detail.title: Documented Jobber and Housecall Pro connections
pros_detail.explanation: Jobber's help center describes syncing approved timesheet hours and reimbursable expenses from Jobber into Gusto (Jobber Connect plan or higher). Housecall Pro lists Gusto on its integrations page.

pros_detail.title: Accounting sync to QuickBooks Online and Xero
pros_detail.explanation: Each payroll run syncs to your books. On Xero, you can split the sync by employee, department, job title or Gusto project and use Xero tracking categories.

pros_detail.title: A plan for 1099-only crews
pros_detail.explanation: Businesses that pay only subcontractors can use the Contractor Only plan at $35/mo + $6/mo per contractor instead of a full payroll plan.

cons_detail.title: Simple is for one state
cons_detail.explanation: Gusto positions Simple for businesses that run payroll in one state. Multi-state payroll starts on Plus at $80/mo + $12/person.

cons_detail.title: Time tracking costs extra on Simple
cons_detail.explanation: Time tracking is included in Plus and Premium; on Simple it is a paid add-on.

cons_detail.title: Per-person fees grow with the crew
cons_detail.explanation: At list prices, 10 people cost $109/mo on Simple and $200/mo on Plus; 25 people cost $199/mo on Simple and $380/mo on Plus.

cons_detail.title: Premium is a large step up
cons_detail.explanation: Premium's dedicated support, HR guidance and same-day or instant pay cost $180/mo + $22/person on Gusto's pricing page, well above Plus at $80/mo + $12/person.

cons_detail.title: Jobber sync covers hourly employees only
cons_detail.explanation: Jobber's help center says salary, contractor and commission employee types cannot sync, timesheets must be approved in Jobber first, and synced hours overwrite existing entries in Gusto.

services.best_for: Trade shops with W-2 employees, 1099 subcontractors or both that want online payroll with automatic tax filing and published prices, especially if they already use QuickBooks Online, Xero, Jobber or Housecall Pro
services.best_team_size: 2-50 employees (our editorial range; Simple covers one state, Plus adds multi-state payroll)
services.weaknesses: Simple covers payroll in one state only, time tracking is a paid add-on on Simple, per-person fees add up as the crew grows, and Premium costs $180/mo + $22/person

ratings.reddit_sentiment: strongly positive: most-recommended SMB payroll in r/smallbusiness, r/HVAC, r/Plumbing

services.affiliate_payout_note: We applied to Gusto's affiliate program (run through Impact) and were not accepted. We have no affiliate relationship with Gusto and earn nothing if you sign up

service_faqs.q: How much does Gusto cost for a 3-person crew?
service_faqs.a: At list prices, Simple is $49 + 3 x $6 = $67/mo and Plus is $80 + 3 x $12 = $116/mo. Simple covers payroll in one state; Plus adds multi-state payroll and time tracking.

service_faqs.q: Does Gusto handle 1099 contractors?
service_faqs.a: Yes. Gusto's pricing page lists a Contractor Only plan at $35/mo + $6/mo per contractor for businesses without W-2 employees. Shops with both employees and subcontractors use Simple, Plus or Premium.

service_faqs.q: Does Gusto work with Jobber and QuickBooks?
service_faqs.a: Yes. Jobber (Connect plan or higher) can send approved timesheet hours and reimbursable expenses for hourly employees into Gusto, and Gusto syncs each payroll run to QuickBooks Online or Xero.

service_faqs.q: Who owns Gusto?
service_faqs.a: Gusto is a privately held company based in San Francisco, incorporated in 2011 as ZenPayroll. It has made acquisitions of its own, completing its purchase of retirement plan provider Guideline in 2025 and announcing the Mosey acquisition in April 2026.

services.name: OnPay
services.tagline: One-plan online payroll at $49/mo plus $6 per person, with QuickBooks and Xero sync and optional pay-as-you-go workers' comp
services.pricing_summary: $49/mo base + $6/person; one core payroll plan with unlimited pay runs and tax filing; optional HR add-on $15/mo + $2/worker; first month free.
services.long_description:
OnPay is an online payroll, HR and benefits provider headquartered in Atlanta. OnPay says it grew out of founder Jesse Burgess's work at his family's payroll business, which he joined in 2007, where he automated tasks for the payroll clerks until he saw the whole process could move online. The company is privately held and venture-backed: in January 2025 it announced more than $100 million in funding, including a $63 million Series B led by Carrick Capital Partners, according to TechCrunch.

OnPay sells one core payroll plan at $49/mo plus $6/mo per person. OnPay says that price includes unlimited pay runs, automated federal, state and local tax filings, garnishment deductions and printable year-end W-2 and 1099 forms. An HR add-on costs $15/mo plus $2/mo per worker and adds tools such as PTO management, customizable workflows and document audits. OnPay advertises the first month free, with free onboarding support and account migration.

On the accounting side, OnPay says it has direct integrations with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop and Xero, and it syncs with time-tracking apps including QuickBooks Time, Deputy and When I Work. Its Xero sync can map payroll lines by department, pay type or tracking category. OnPay also offers pay-as-you-go workers' comp that adjusts premiums based on actual payroll data, and in 2026 it announced a 401(k) integration with Betterment at Work and a partnership with Ramp.

The trade-off: we could not confirm a direct integration with a field-service app such as Jobber or Housecall Pro (Housecall Pro's integrations page lists Gusto as its payroll integration), so crew hours may need to come through a supported time-tracking app or be keyed in. HR tools beyond the core plan cost extra, and the per-person fee grows with the crew.
services.how_it_works: Sign up on OnPay's website; OnPay says it provides free onboarding support and account migration from your old provider. Add company, bank and employee or contractor details, then run payroll as often as you need; OnPay calculates and pays wages and files federal, state and local payroll taxes. Hours can come in from QuickBooks Time, Deputy or When I Work, and each payroll syncs to QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop or Xero. Year-end W-2 and 1099 forms are included. The HR add-on and pay-as-you-go workers' comp are optional extras.

pros_detail.title: One core plan with a published price
pros_detail.explanation: OnPay's pricing page lists $49/mo + $6/mo per person for payroll with unlimited pay runs, automated federal, state and local tax filings, garnishment deductions and year-end W-2 and 1099 forms.

pros_detail.title: First month free with migration help
pros_detail.explanation: OnPay advertises the first month free, with full access to payroll and HR tools during that month, plus free onboarding support and account migration.

pros_detail.title: Accounting and time-tracking integrations
pros_detail.explanation: OnPay says it integrates directly with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop and Xero, and syncs hours from QuickBooks Time, Deputy and When I Work.

pros_detail.title: Pay-as-you-go workers' comp option
pros_detail.explanation: OnPay offers workers' comp that adjusts premiums based on actual payroll data, which suits trades whose payroll swings with the season.

pros_detail.title: 401(k) through Betterment at Work
pros_detail.explanation: In May 2026 OnPay and Betterment at Work announced a 401(k) integration for small businesses.

cons_detail.title: HR tools cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: PTO management, customizable workflows and document audits sit in the HR add-on at $15/mo + $2/mo per worker.

cons_detail.title: No field-service app integration confirmed
cons_detail.explanation: We could not confirm a direct OnPay integration with Jobber or Housecall Pro; Housecall Pro's integrations page lists Gusto as its payroll integration. Hours may need to come through a supported time-tracking app or be keyed in.

cons_detail.title: Per-person fees grow with the crew
cons_detail.explanation: At list price, 10 people cost $109/mo and 25 people cost $199/mo before any add-ons.

services.best_for: Small trade shops that want one published payroll price, QuickBooks or Xero sync and an optional pay-as-you-go workers' comp policy, and that can live without a direct field-service app integration
services.weaknesses: HR tools are a paid add-on, no direct field-service app integration was confirmed, and per-person fees add up as the crew grows

ratings.reddit_sentiment: positive: 'cheaper Gusto with same core features' is a common refrain

services.affiliate_payout_note: Direct publisher affiliate program with per-signup payouts in $100-$200 range

service_faqs.q: How does OnPay compare to Gusto on price?
service_faqs.a: Both list $49/mo + $6/person for their entry payroll plan (OnPay's core plan and Gusto Simple). Gusto positions Simple for payroll in one state and sells higher tiers; OnPay sells one core payroll plan and charges separately for its HR add-on ($15/mo + $2/worker).

service_faqs.a: OnPay advertises the first month free, with free onboarding support and account migration. Its Xero app store listing describes this as a 30-day free trial.

service_faqs.q: Can OnPay handle workers' comp?
service_faqs.a: OnPay offers pay-as-you-go workers' comp that adjusts premiums based on actual payroll data. Premiums are not published; they depend on your business.

services.name: Patriot Payroll
services.tagline: Low-cost online payroll from Canton, Ohio: $37/mo plus $5 per worker with full tax filing, or $17/mo plus $4 per worker if you file taxes yourself
services.pricing_summary: From $17/mo + $4/worker (Basic, you file taxes); Full Service $37/mo + $5/worker with tax filing in one state; each extra state $12/mo; 30-day free trial, then 50% off for 3 months.
services.long_description:
Patriot Software is a Canton, Ohio company that sells online payroll and accounting software to small businesses. The Better Business Bureau lists Patriot Software LLC as started in August 2002, with Kyle Dreger as CEO. We found no report of Patriot being acquired.

Patriot sells two payroll plans. Basic Payroll is $17/mo plus $4 per worker paid in the month; Patriot calculates payroll but does not deposit or file payroll taxes, so you file forms such as Form 941 and make the tax deposits yourself. Full Service Payroll is $37/mo plus $5 per worker paid, and Patriot collects, deposits and files federal, state and local taxes, including year-end filings. Full Service covers one state; each additional state is $12/mo. Optional add-ons are Time & Attendance ($6/mo plus $2 per employee who uses a time card), HR Software ($6/mo plus $2 per W-2 employee paid) and HR Experts and Training ($45/mo).

Patriot offers a 30-day free trial followed by 50% off for 3 months. A credit card is required during the trial, but Patriot says you are not billed until the trial ends and can cancel at any time without penalty. Routine support is free by phone, chat and email, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Eastern Time, from what Patriot calls a U.S.-based support team.

Patriot payroll integrates directly with QuickBooks Online and with Patriot's own accounting software. QuickBooks Desktop users export payroll through an IIF file rather than a live sync. Patriot also offers free integrations with Vestwell for 401(k) plans, SimplyInsured for health benefits, and a partner for pay-as-you-go workers' comp in states that allow it.

The trade-off: the per-worker fees are low, but Basic leaves tax deposits and filings to you, crews working in more than one state add $12/mo per extra state, and time tracking and HR tools are add-ons. We found no Xero integration and no field-service app integration (such as Jobber or Housecall Pro) in Patriot's help center.
services.how_it_works: Start the 30-day free trial on Patriot's website; a credit card is required, but billing starts only after the trial. The setup wizard asks for company tax IDs, employee information, state unemployment rates, paycheck printing preferences and payment details. Choose Basic (you deposit and file payroll taxes) or Full Service (Patriot collects, deposits and files federal, state and local taxes, including year-end filings). Each pay period, enter hours or bring them in from the Time & Attendance add-on, then approve payroll. Payroll can post to QuickBooks Online or Patriot Accounting, or be exported to QuickBooks Desktop as an IIF file.

pros_detail.title: Full tax handling on Full Service

pros_detail.title: 30-day free trial, then 50% off for 3 months

pros_detail.title: Free U.S.-based support
pros_detail.explanation: Routine support is free by phone, chat and email, weekdays 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Eastern Time.

pros_detail.title: Free benefits and workers' comp integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Patriot connects to Vestwell for 401(k) plans, SimplyInsured for health benefits and a pay-as-you-go workers' comp partner in states that allow it.

cons_detail.title: Basic leaves taxes to you
cons_detail.explanation: On Basic, you file payroll forms such as Form 941 and make the tax deposits yourself.

cons_detail.title: Extra states cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Full Service includes one state; each additional state is $12/mo, which adds up for crews that work across state lines.

cons_detail.title: Time tracking and HR are add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Time & Attendance is $6/mo + $2 per employee using a time card, HR Software is $6/mo + $2 per W-2 employee paid, and HR Experts and Training is $45/mo.

cons_detail.title: Few accounting and field-service integrations
cons_detail.explanation: Direct sync is limited to QuickBooks Online and Patriot Accounting, QuickBooks Desktop uses an IIF file export, and we found no Xero, Jobber or Housecall Pro integration in Patriot's help center.

services.weaknesses: Basic leaves tax deposits and filings to you, each extra state adds $12/mo, time tracking and HR tools are paid add-ons, and accounting integrations are limited to QuickBooks and Patriot's own software

service_faqs.a: At list prices for 3 workers, Patriot Full Service is $37 + 3 x $5 = $52/mo, while Gusto Simple and OnPay are each $49 + 3 x $6 = $67/mo. Patriot Basic is $17 + 3 x $4 = $29/mo but does not deposit or file your payroll taxes.

service_faqs.q: Should I pick Basic or Full Service?
service_faqs.a: Basic suits owners (or their accountant) who will deposit payroll taxes and file forms such as Form 941 themselves. Full Service costs $20/mo more in base fee plus $1 more per worker, and Patriot handles federal, state and local deposits and filings, including year-end filings.

services.name: Hourly.io
services.tagline: Payroll plus pay-as-you-go workers' comp in one app, with GPS time tracking and job costing on every plan
services.pricing_summary: From $80/mo + $12/active user (Gold, four-day direct deposit); Platinum $120/mo + $16/user with next-day deposit after 8 qualifying runs and credit approval; Platinum+ with same-day deposit is quoted.
services.long_description:
Hourly (Hourly, Inc.) combines payroll with pay-as-you-go workers' comp insurance in one platform. SEC Form D filings list Hourly, Inc. as a Delaware corporation incorporated in 2019 with its principal place of business in Palo Alto, California; its 2022 filing reports about $27 million sold in a funding round. Tom Sagi is co-founder and CEO. Hourly says it is not a PEO: it does not lease your employees, and it shows what you pay for each part.

Hourly describes its workers' comp as pay-as-you-go: premiums are paid automatically based on your actual payroll, calculated as payroll (per $100) times the class code rate times your experience modifier, plus state taxes and fees. Hourly says coverage is provided by carriers rated A+ (Superior) by AM Best and that policies under $5,000 get a streamlined audit with minimal paperwork. You can generate your own certificate of insurance from your phone, and you can buy workers' comp and payroll together or start with one.

Payroll comes in three plans. Gold is $80/mo plus $12 per active user with four-day direct deposit. Platinum is $120/mo plus $16 per active user with next-day direct deposit, and Platinum+ is quoted ('Exclusive Pricing') with same-day direct deposit; next-day and same-day deposit are available after 8 qualifying payroll runs and credit approval. Every plan includes automated tax payments and filing, W-2s, garnishments and child support payments, the workers' comp integration, an employee app, GPS time tracking, job costing reports, unlimited payroll runs and unlimited phone support. Platinum adds a dedicated customer success team, next-day paper check delivery, paperless onboarding and unlimited HR expert access. Hourly bills only for active users: anyone who records at least one shift or is paid at least once in the month.

The trade-off: Gold's four-day direct deposit is slower than the next-day deposit on QuickBooks' base Workforce Payroll plan, faster deposit needs a pricier tier plus a payroll track record, and $12-$16 per user is double or more the $6 per person that Gusto Simple and OnPay charge. Hourly's pages do not list the states where its workers' comp is sold, so confirm your state first. Pay-as-you-go workers' comp is also available through partners at other payroll services, including OnPay and Patriot, so compare the full package rather than the idea alone.
services.how_it_works: Contact Hourly or sign up on its website. For workers' comp, the premium depends on your class codes, payroll, experience modifier and the states where your team works. Once set up, your crew clocks in on Hourly's employee app with GPS time tracking, you run payroll, and Hourly makes the tax payments and filings and pays workers by direct deposit or paper check. Each payroll run also pays the workers' comp premium on that payroll, so the premium follows actual wages instead of an up-front estimate. Job costing reports break down labor cost, and you are billed only for workers who record a shift or get paid that month.

pros_detail.title: Workers' comp premiums follow actual payroll
pros_detail.explanation: Hourly collects the premium with each payroll run, calculated as payroll (per $100) times your class code rate times your experience modifier, plus state taxes and fees, instead of an up-front estimate.

pros_detail.title: Payroll and workers' comp in one place
pros_detail.explanation: The same platform runs payroll and the policy. Hourly says you can buy both or start with one and switch the other later.

pros_detail.title: GPS time tracking and job costing on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: All plans include GPS time tracking, job costing reports, unlimited payroll runs, automated tax filing and unlimited phone support.

pros_detail.title: Billing only for active users
pros_detail.explanation: Hourly charges the per-user fee only for people who record at least one shift or get paid at least once in the month, which suits seasonal crews.

pros_detail.title: 90-day refund offer
pros_detail.explanation: Hourly says it will refund 100% of the subscription cost for the first 90 days of service if the platform doesn't meet your needs.

cons_detail.title: Four-day direct deposit on Gold
cons_detail.explanation: Gold pays by four-day direct deposit. Next-day (Platinum) and same-day (Platinum+) deposit need a pricier plan, 8 qualifying payroll runs and credit approval.

cons_detail.title: Higher per-user fees
cons_detail.explanation: Gold is $12 and Platinum $16 per active user per month, against $6 per person on Gusto Simple and OnPay.

cons_detail.title: No published state list
cons_detail.explanation: Hourly's pages do not list the states where its workers' comp is sold; cost depends on where your team works, so confirm your state before switching.

cons_detail.title: Top tier is quote-only
cons_detail.explanation: Platinum+ with same-day deposit is shown as 'Exclusive Pricing' with no published price.

cons_detail.title: Thin accounting integration detail
cons_detail.explanation: Hourly's accounting page names QuickBooks without saying which version or what syncs, and we found no Xero integration.

services.best_for: Trade shops paying hourly field crews that want workers' comp premiums tied to each payroll run, with GPS time tracking and job costing in the same app
services.weaknesses: Four-day direct deposit on the Gold plan, higher per-user fees than payroll-only services, a quote-only top tier, and no published list of states where its workers' comp is sold

ratings.reddit_sentiment: positive among trades contractors specifically: 'finally a WC solution that doesn't shock me at audit' is the recurring refrain

services.affiliate_payout_note: Direct affiliate program with per-signup payouts

service_faqs.q: Is Hourly available in my state?
service_faqs.a: Hourly's pricing and workers' comp pages do not list the states where its workers' comp is sold, and Hourly says cost depends on the states where your team works. Its licenses page lists insurance brokerage licenses by state. Ask Hourly before you switch.

service_faqs.q: How does the pay-as-you-go workers' comp work?
service_faqs.a: Each payroll run pays the premium on that payroll: payroll (per $100) times your class code rate times your experience modifier, plus state taxes and fees. Hourly says policies under $5,000 get a streamlined audit with minimal paperwork.

service_faqs.q: Do I have to buy both payroll and workers' comp?
service_faqs.a: No. Hourly recommends both to get the full benefit, but says you can start with one and switch the other when the timing suits you.

services.name: QuickBooks Payroll (plans branded QuickBooks Workforce)
services.tagline: Intuit's own payroll, now sold as QuickBooks Workforce: runs inside QuickBooks Online, from $50/mo plus $7 per employee payroll-only
services.pricing_summary: From $50/mo + $7/employee (Workforce Payroll, payroll only); Workforce Premium $88/mo + $13/employee; Workforce Elite $134/mo + $17/employee; bundles with QuickBooks Online accounting from $88/mo + $6.50/employee; 50% off the base fee for 3 months was offered at our September 30, 2026 check.
services.long_description:
QuickBooks Payroll is Intuit's payroll service for QuickBooks users, now sold under the QuickBooks Workforce name. In its 2026 annual report, Intuit describes QuickBooks Workforce as an all-in-one HR and payroll platform for small and mid-market businesses that integrates with QuickBooks Online. Intuit is a public company headquartered in Mountain View, California, and its payroll page says QuickBooks serves 1.4 million businesses for payroll and tax management.

There are three payroll-only plans. Workforce Payroll is $50/mo plus $7 per employee and includes full-service payroll, next-day direct deposit, 1099 e-filing, basic team management and an employee portal. Workforce Premium is $88/mo plus $13 per employee and adds same-day direct deposit, an expert review of your setup, time tracking, scheduling and more HR tools. Workforce Elite is $134/mo plus $17 per employee and adds expert setup, tax penalty protection (Intuit says up to $25,000), a personal HR advisor, geofencing and mileage tracking. Intuit says every plan includes Payroll AI, which collects time and attendance data, spots inconsistencies and texts the admin, and there is no annual contract.

Bundles with QuickBooks Online accounting are also sold: Workforce Payroll with Simple Start at $88/mo plus $6.50 per employee, with Essentials at $125/mo plus $6.50 per employee, and Workforce Premium with Plus (which includes project tracking) at $203/mo plus $10 per employee. At our September 30, 2026 check, every plan and bundle was offered at 50% off the base fee for 3 months.

Intuit also lists health insurance (medical, dental and vision through Allstate), 401(k) plans through Vestwell, workers' comp options, HR advisor access through Mineral and background checks through Checkr from $29.99 per report. Payroll phone support runs Monday to Friday, 5 a.m. to 6 p.m. Pacific.

The trade-off: at list prices a 5-employee shop pays $85/mo for Workforce Payroll against $79/mo for Gusto Simple or OnPay, and the gap grows with headcount ($7 against $6 per person). Time tracking starts on Premium, tax penalty protection only comes with Elite, and the pricing pages showed a buy-now discount rather than a free trial. The main reason to choose it is that payroll lives inside your QuickBooks Online account.
services.how_it_works: Buy a payroll-only plan or a bundle with QuickBooks Online accounting on Intuit's website. Add employees and contractors; employees get a portal and can use the Workforce mobile app. Each pay period, QuickBooks calculates pay and taxes, pays by direct deposit (next-day on Workforce Payroll, same-day on Premium and Elite) and handles payroll tax filings; auto payroll can run salaried payrolls on schedule. On Premium and Elite, time tracking feeds payroll. Because Workforce integrates with QuickBooks Online, payroll costs post to the same QuickBooks account you use for your books.

pros_detail.title: Built into QuickBooks Online
pros_detail.explanation: Intuit says Workforce integrates with QuickBooks Online, and bundles combine payroll and accounting in one subscription, so there is no separate payroll vendor to connect.

pros_detail.title: Next-day direct deposit on the base plan
pros_detail.explanation: Workforce Payroll includes next-day direct deposit; Premium and Elite add same-day direct deposit.

pros_detail.title: Tax penalty protection on Elite
pros_detail.explanation: Intuit says Workforce Elite includes tax penalty protection of up to $25,000, along with expert setup and a personal HR advisor.

pros_detail.title: Benefits and HR options from one vendor
pros_detail.explanation: Intuit lists health insurance through Allstate, 401(k) plans through Vestwell, workers' comp options and HR advisor access through Mineral.

services.long_description:
Square Payroll is the payroll service of Square, part of Block, Inc. Block says it started the Square ecosystem in February 2009 to let businesses accept card payments. The company uses a distributed work model and says it has no formal headquarters; its SEC filings list an Oakland, California address as its principal executive office. Block's 2025 annual report names Square Payroll and Square Team Management among the operational tools it offers sellers.

Full-service payroll costs $35/mo plus $6 per person paid. Square says it includes automated federal and state tax payments and filings (quarterly and annual), year-end W-2 and 1099-NEC filings, unlimited pay runs, auto payroll, off-cycle payments, multistate payroll, multiple pay rates, and two-day, four-day or next-day direct deposit; Instant Payments can pay the team the same day from Square account funds. Contractor-only payroll is $6 per person paid with no base fee, but it leaves out automated tax payments and filings, auto payroll and multistate payroll. There are no long-term contracts. If you want paper W-2s or 1099s mailed, Square charges $3 per person per year.

The payroll connects to the rest of Square: time tracked with Square POS and Square's team tools feeds payroll, and the full-service plan adds direct-tip tracking and importing, overtime calculations and labor-cost reporting. Square says payroll can sync to QuickBooks Online. Health insurance, 401(k) plans and workers' comp are available, with workers' comp listed as an add-on on both plans.

The trade-off: much of the value comes from already running your business on Square. Square's payroll pages name QuickBooks Online and Square's own tools, not field-service apps such as Jobber or Housecall Pro. The contractor-only plan is inexpensive because it skips tax filings and multistate support.
services.how_it_works: Sign up from an existing Square account or a new one and add employees and contractors. Hours tracked through Square POS or Square's team tools flow into payroll, where Square calculates pay and taxes. On full-service payroll, Square pays and files federal and state payroll taxes and files W-2s and 1099-NECs at year end; you choose two-day, four-day or next-day direct deposit, or Instant Payments from Square funds. Contractor-only payroll pays 1099 workers and delivers forms digitally but does not include automated tax payments and filings. Payroll can sync to QuickBooks Online.

services.long_description:
Rippling is a workforce platform that combines HR, IT and finance tools with payroll. Rippling describes itself as a platform that unifies HR, IT, finance and more on a single source of truth for employee data, and says it integrates with 600+ apps. Its product list includes HRIS, payroll, benefits administration, time and attendance, scheduling, recruiting, performance and learning management, device management, identity and access management, expenses, corporate cards, bill pay, travel, global payroll and employer of record.

Rippling does not publish prices. Its pricing page is a quote request form, and its FAQ says most Rippling products are billed per employee per month, that some may be charged at (or include) a monthly base fee, and that each HR, finance and IT product can be purchased separately. You tell Rippling which products you need and it sends a custom quote.

For payroll itself, Rippling says it calculates payroll taxes and files them with federal, state and local agencies, that HR data such as new hires, salary changes and benefits deductions flows into payroll automatically, and that it integrates with accounting systems including QuickBooks, Xero and NetSuite. Its payroll page does not mention certified payroll, prevailing-wage reporting or job costing, so a contractor doing public work should ask about those before signing.

The trade-off: Rippling is built to run many HR, IT and finance functions in one place, which suits a growing company with office staff, laptops and several benefit plans to manage. A small trades shop that only needs to pay a crew and file payroll taxes will be paying for a platform built around much more than that, and it cannot compare the cost until it has a quote.
services.how_it_works: Request a quote or a demo, choose the products you need (for a trades shop, usually payroll plus time and attendance and possibly benefits), and Rippling prices them per employee per month. Employee records live in one system, and Rippling says changes such as new hires, raises and benefits deductions flow into payroll automatically. Rippling says it calculates payroll taxes and files them with federal, state and local agencies. Other products, such as device management or expense cards, can be added later on the same platform.

services.tagline: ADP's small-business payroll for 1-49 employees, priced by quote in four packages
services.pricing_summary: Quote only; ADP publishes no RUN prices. services.long_description:
RUN Powered by ADP is ADP's payroll and HR product for small businesses. ADP pitches it at companies with 1-49 employees, and ADP's fiscal 2026 annual report (Form 10-K) says RUN serves over 980,000 small businesses. ADP itself dates to 1949 and is headquartered in Roseland, New Jersey.

ADP does not publish RUN prices. The product and package pages send you to a Get Pricing form or a sales line for a quote. RUN comes in four packages: Essential Payroll (payroll, tax filing, direct deposit, reporting, employee access and 24/7 support), Enhanced Payroll (adds check signing, state unemployment insurance management, job costing, labor law poster compliance and ZipRecruiter job posting), Complete Payroll & HR Plus (adds an HR HelpDesk, employee handbook wizard, HR tracking and a forms library) and HR Pro Payroll & HR (adds applicant tracking, a learning management system, harassment prevention training and legal assistance services). Time and attendance, retirement, workers' compensation and health insurance are add-ons.

ADP says RUN files federal, state and local payroll taxes, includes multi-jurisdiction payroll in every package, offers a mobile app and an assistant called ADP Assist that flags errors, and exports journal entries to QuickBooks, Xero, Wave and Creative Solutions. The package page says you do not have to sign a contract and services can be terminated at any time. Through October 22, 2026, ADP is offering new RUN clients with 1-49 employees in the continental US three months of free payroll processing, applied to invoices in months four through six, with conditions set out in the offer terms.

The trade-off: RUN gives a small trades shop job costing (from the Enhanced package up), add-on time tracking and workers' comp, and a large payroll company behind the tax filing, but you cannot see a price until you talk to ADP. Get the quote in writing, including which package it covers and what happens to the price after any promotional months, and compare it with services that publish their prices.
services.how_it_works: Request pricing through ADP's form or sales line, pick a package, and ADP sets up your account. You then run payroll on a computer, in the mobile app or by phone. ADP calculates and files federal, state and local payroll taxes, pays employees by direct deposit or on a Wisely pay card, and can export journal entries to QuickBooks, Xero, Wave or Creative Solutions. ADP says no contract is required and service can be terminated at any time.

services.how_it_works: Talk to Paychex's sales team or request pricing online, choose the modules you need, and Paychex sets up payroll on the Flex platform. services.tagline: PEO and payroll provider for small businesses: co-employment that bundles payroll, benefits, workers' comp and HR
services.pricing_summary: Payroll plan $50/mo base + $8/employee; PEO Basic $79/employee/mo and PEO Plus $124/employee/mo with no base fee; global EOR $599/employee/mo; add-ons such as time tracking ($8/employee/mo) cost extra.
services.long_description:
Justworks is a New York company, incorporated in 2012 as Clockwork Solutions, that is best known as a professional employer organization (PEO) for small businesses. In a PEO, the provider becomes a co-employer of your staff: Justworks' 2021 IPO filing (the IPO was later withdrawn) explains that a PEO groups the employees of many small businesses under its own federal employer identification number and files employment taxes on a consolidated basis. Justworks markets both a PEO and a payroll service, and in 2023 it agreed to acquire Via, an international employment platform, to expand hiring outside the US.

According to that 2021 filing, the Justworks PEO covered payroll, benefits, compliance and risk management, including workers' compensation coverage, payroll tax filings, W-2 processing, employment practices liability insurance and state unemployment insurance filings. It offered access to national health insurance from three major carriers plus dental, vision, 401(k), FSAs and HSAs, 24/7 support, and tools for onboarding, paid time off and time and attendance. At the time Justworks reported over 8,000 customers in all 50 states. Check Justworks' current plan pages for what each plan includes today.

Justworks publishes its prices. Its Payroll plan, without co-employment, is $50/mo plus $8 per employee; PEO Basic is $79 and PEO Plus $124 per employee per month with no base fee; and its global employer-of-record service is $599 per employee per month. Add-ons include time tracking at $8 per employee and US contractor payments at $8 per paid contractor. Because the per-employee PEO fee covers benefits access, insurance and HR support as well as payroll, the monthly total for a crew can be well above a payroll-only service, so compare the full monthly bill for your headcount.

The trade-off: a PEO can give a small shop access to group health benefits and bundled workers' comp and HR compliance without hiring HR staff, but you share the employer role with Justworks, your benefits come from its plans, and your workers' comp runs through its program. Before signing, ask how Justworks classifies your trade for workers' comp and how it handles a mix of W-2 employees and 1099 subcontractors.
services.how_it_works: Choose a Justworks plan and move your employees onto its platform. On a PEO plan, Justworks becomes a co-employer: it runs payroll and files employment taxes under its own federal employer ID, and provides access to its health, dental, vision and 401(k) plans, workers' comp coverage and HR compliance support. You keep running your business and directing your crew. Fees are charged per employee per month.

services.long_description:
Roll by ADP is ADP's chat-based payroll app for small businesses. ADP launched it in February 2021, describing it in its annual report as a mobile-first solution with an AI-powered chat interface that turns payroll into a conversation. You open the app, type a request such as "payroll", add hours, and Roll's assistant walks you through the run. ADP now describes Roll as using generative AI and offering smart HR assistance.

Pricing is published: $39 a month for the whole company plus $5 per W-2 employee or 1099 contractor. Roll's pricing page says that includes unlimited payroll runs, taxes calculated, deducted and paid for you, payroll in all 50 states, same-day and next-day direct deposit, tracking worker hours, a QuickBooks Online integration, new hire reporting, an employee self-service app, AI-driven error checks, payroll reports and unlimited live chat support, with no long-term contracts. Roll's terms say there may be fees for added services or features you choose.

New US customers who have never used Roll get three months free. Under Roll's terms, the free period starts once you finish company setup and accept the terms; if you start payroll and then cancel during the free period, you forfeit the rest of it, and billing at $39 plus $5 per worker starts automatically with the next monthly cycle after it ends. You cancel through the in-app chat.

The trade-off: Roll keeps payroll simple and priced in the open, with unlimited runs that suit weekly pay, and it is built for owners who run the business from a phone, though desktop access is available. It is a payroll app rather than a full HR suite, so shops that want benefits administration, scheduling or job costing should compare broader platforms.

To run payroll, type a request such as "payroll" and add hours; Roll calculates pay, deducts and pays taxes, and pays W-2 employees and 1099 contractors by direct deposit, with same-day and next-day options. Employees see pay stubs and tax statements in the app. After the free period, billing is $39 a month plus $5 per worker, and you can cancel through the in-app chat.

services.long_description:
Wave Payroll is the payroll add-on of Wave, a small-business money app run by Wave Financial Inc. that offers a free Starter plan for accounting and invoicing and a paid Pro plan. Wave started in 2010 in Toronto, and H&R Block completed its acquisition of the company on July 1, 2019. Wave's site describes the company as Canadian and backed by H&R Block, and says it has helped more than 5.9 million small business owners in the US and Canada since 2010.

Pricing is simple. Wave's payroll page lists one US price for new payroll customers who signed up after April 2, 2025: $40 a month plus $6 per active employee and $6 per independent contractor paid. Wave says its tax service covers all 50 states, so the price is the same in every state. In Canada the price is $25 CAD a month plus $6 per active employee and $6 per contractor paid, in every province and territory except Quebec.

Wave lists unlimited free direct deposits, automatic payroll tax payments and filings, W-2 and 1099-NEC forms, an employee portal for pay stubs and tax forms, leave tracking and accruals, and payroll journal entries that post automatically to Wave's accounting. The payroll page does not mention time tracking, scheduling, job costing, benefits administration or workers' compensation, so a crew that clocks in on job sites needs a separate time app.

For a solo operator or small crew that already keeps its books in Wave, running payroll in the same account saves re-entering wages and taxes by hand.

The trade-off: it is a basic payroll tool with no time tracking or HR features, it only covers the US and Canada, and each contractor paid costs $6 on top of the base fee, so a shop paying 5 employees and 3 subcontractors in a month pays $88.
services.how_it_works: You add Payroll to your Wave account, set up employees, contractors and pay schedules, and run payroll online. Wave pays people by direct deposit, calculates payroll taxes and, under its tax service, pays and files them for you in all 50 states; wages and taxes post to Wave's accounting as journal entries. Employees see pay stubs and tax forms in a self-service portal, and Wave generates W-2 and 1099-NEC forms. Wave says you can use Payroll for up to 30 days commitment-free after your first payroll run.

services.long_description:
Homebase is a team-management app for small businesses with hourly workers. It combines employee scheduling, a time clock, team messaging, hiring, onboarding, HR tools and payroll. Homebase says more than 100,000 small businesses use it. The company, legally Pioneer Works, Inc., lists a San Francisco mailing address and offices in Houston, Denver and Toronto, and was co-founded by John Waldmann and Rushi Patel.

The team-management plans are priced per location. Basic is free for one location with up to 10 employees; Essentials is $30, Plus $70 and All-in-One $120 per location per month on monthly billing, each with unlimited employees, and Homebase says annual billing saves 20%. Payroll is an add-on available on any plan, including Basic, at $49 a month plus $6 per employee paid. Homebase offers a 14-day free trial of All-in-One with no credit card.

For a crew, the useful part is the link between the clock and the paycheck. Workers clock in on a phone, tablet or POS device, with GPS and photo capture at clock-in, and Homebase tracks overtime and breaks. The payroll add-on runs payroll from those timesheets, with automated tax calculation, payments and filings, and Homebase says payroll is available to US businesses in all 50 states and Washington, D.C. Shops that keep another payroll provider can sync hours to QuickBooks, Gusto, ADP, Paychex and others listed on its integrations page.

The trade-off: Homebase is built around hourly shift work, and its pages do not mention job costing or certified payroll. Payroll and several tools (tip management, task management, background checks, a hiring assistant) cost extra, and per-location pricing adds up for shops with several locations.

The payroll add-on ($49/month plus $6 per employee paid) runs payroll from those timesheets, calculates, pays and files payroll taxes, and pays people by direct deposit or printable check. services.long_description:
TriNet is a professional employer organization (PEO). Through co-employment, TriNet takes on responsibility for paying wages to your employees, providing workers' compensation insurance and giving access to group health, welfare and retirement benefits, while you keep running the daily work. TriNet was founded in 1988 and is headquartered in Dublin, California. It reported about 323,200 worksite employees at the end of 2025, says it has held ESAC accreditation since 1995, and says a TriNet subsidiary is an IRS Certified Professional Employer Organization.

For a growing trades business, the pitch is benefits and paperwork in one place: group medical, dental and vision plans, a TriNet-sponsored 401(k), payroll with payroll tax administration, HR compliance support, and pay-as-you-go workers' comp plans with no deposits or deductibles. TriNet also sells HR Plus, an administrative services (ASO) option for companies that want HR software and support without a PEO.

TriNet does not publish list prices. It charges a flat fee per employee per month, quoted based on company size, industry, location and services, and bills benefits premiums, workers' compensation costs, payroll taxes and add-ons on top. It also requires a minimum number of worksite employees, which it does not publish.

TriNet's annual report names its main industry verticals as technology, financial services, life sciences, nonprofit, professional services and main street businesses. A contractor should ask how its workers' comp class codes are handled before comparing quotes.

The trade-off: a PEO costs more than a payroll-only service because the fee bundles HR and benefits administration, prices come only by quote, and co-employment means sharing some employer responsibilities and HR processes with TriNet. A shop that only needs to pay people and file taxes is better served by a payroll tool.

TriNet then takes on responsibility for paying wages, providing workers' compensation insurance and giving your employees access to its group health, welfare and retirement benefits, while you direct the daily work. services.long_description:
Fingercheck is a payroll, time-tracking and HR platform for businesses whose crews work away from a desk. It describes itself as Brooklyn-built since 2013, and its privacy policy lists FingerCheck LLC at 300 Kent Ave in Brooklyn, New York. In October 2024 Edison Partners led a $115 million growth investment in the company, joined by StepStone Group and Columbus Capital, and Dan Kazan was named CEO. Fingercheck says it has served more than 5,000 companies.

The construction features are the draw for trades. Fingercheck says it captures GPS-verified hours and assigns them to the right job code, so you can see labor cost by job. It generates certified payroll as Form WH-347 and NYC Certified Payroll Report PDFs filled from your payroll data, and lets you set prevailing wages at the worker and job-site level for public construction projects. Crews can punch in by app, fingerprint, SMS or facial recognition, with mobile geofencing, and hours sync to payroll without re-entry.

Pricing is published. Time & Attendance is $29 a month plus $7 per employee but has no payroll. The 360 plan, $79 a month plus $10 per employee, adds unlimited payroll, multi-state tax calculation, hiring and onboarding, and certified payroll reports. 360 Plus, $129 a month plus $12 per employee, adds next-day pay, team chat, credential management and benefits administration, and 360 Pro is custom-quoted. The first three plans carry a minimum spend equal to 5 employees, and Fingercheck says there are no long-term contracts.

For a construction or field-heavy trades business that works prevailing-wage jobs or wants labor cost by job, Fingercheck puts time tracking, job codes, certified payroll and payroll in one system.

The trade-off: the cheapest plan has no payroll, certified payroll starts on the 360 plan, and the 5-employee minimum means a two-person shop pays at least $129 a month on 360. It is also a combined time, payroll and HR system, so switching means moving all three.
services.how_it_works: Field workers punch in and out by app, fingerprint, SMS or facial recognition, with mobile geofencing, and Fingercheck assigns GPS-verified hours to job codes so you can track labor cost by job. Approved hours sync straight into payroll in the same system. On the 360 plan and above, Fingercheck runs unlimited payroll with multi-state tax calculation and generates certified payroll reports (Form WH-347 and the NYC Certified Payroll Report) for government construction projects. You pay monthly per plan, with no long-term contract and a minimum spend equal to 5 employees.

services.long_description:
eBacon is cloud payroll and HR software built for construction contractors, with its focus on certified payroll and prevailing-wage compliance. The company says it was founded in 2003 by Jack Biltis and Ron Bleich after conversations with California construction firms about the Davis-Bacon Act, and it is based in Phoenix, Arizona.

The core is payroll for public and prevailing-wage jobs. eBacon says it calculates paychecks and taxes, files federal and state payroll tax returns, pre-fills federal and state WH-347 certified payroll reports from project data, and assigns worker classifications and pay rates from what it describes as more than 187,000 pre-loaded wage determinations. It supports union payroll, multi-state work, job costing with general ledger export, garnishments and back-wage restitution, plus a mobile time app for iOS and Android with GPS clock-in.

Fringe handling is a distinct piece. eBacon administers a bona fide fringe trust that turns prevailing-wage fringe obligations into pre-tax contributions such as 401(k), HRA or FSA accounts, and workers can choose a weekly cash payout or keep the money in the trust. It also offers HR tools (onboarding, certification and training tracking), 401(k) administration and workers' comp tracking.

The trade-off: eBacon publishes no prices, so cost is only known after a demo and quote, and its value is concentrated in prevailing-wage and government-funded work. A contractor that never bids those jobs gets little from the certified-payroll and fringe features and can use a general payroll tool; one that does should compare it with other construction payroll providers such as Payroll4Construction and Miter.

Crews clock time on the mobile app or it is entered against jobs, and eBacon applies the prevailing-wage rates and fringe, calculates pay and taxes, pays by direct deposit or pay card, files federal and state payroll tax returns and pre-fills WH-347 certified payroll reports. Labor costs export to your general ledger (eBacon names QuickBooks Desktop and Sage 100 among its options). Pricing is quoted after a demo.

Arcoro is a time tracking, HR and payroll platform built for construction companies. It says it has served the construction industry since 2018 and is based in Phoenix, Arizona. The company brought together ExakTime, a construction time-clock product now sold as Arcoro Time, and HR software including the former InfinityHR system, and it is backed by private equity firm PSG (Providence Strategic Growth). Arcoro says more than 7,000 companies use it.

The platform is modular. Hiring covers applicant tracking and digital onboarding, including a job-site kiosk mode. Day-to-day tools include GPS-verified time tracking, an HR system of record, benefits and payroll. Development tools cover learning management for safety training, certifications and OSHA compliance, plus performance and succession planning. Arcoro also lists I-9 verification, multi-state compliance and certification tracking, and in July 2026 it launched a single mobile app where workers clock in and see pay stubs, benefits and HR information.

Payroll is now part of Arcoro itself. It says it handles monthly, quarterly and annual tax filings, sets prevailing-wage rates, exports certified payroll data for WH-347 and LCPtracker reporting, handles union deductions and maps payroll to your general ledger and job costs. Its integration page names Acumatica, CMiC, Sage 100, Sage 300, Sage Intacct, Foundation Software, Procore, Viewpoint Vista and Viewpoint Spectrum.

The trade-off: Arcoro publishes no prices, so you get a custom proposal after a demo, and the full suite is more than a small shop that only needs to pay a crew will use. It fits contractors that want hiring, safety training, time tracking and payroll in one construction-focused system and use one of the accounting or ERP systems it connects to.
services.how_it_works: You choose the Arcoro modules you need (applicant tracking, onboarding, time tracking, HR, benefits, payroll, learning, performance) and Arcoro builds a custom proposal. Crews clock in with GPS verification on the mobile app, and that time feeds payroll, which applies prevailing-wage and union rules, files payroll taxes and exports certified payroll data for WH-347 and LCPtracker. Payroll and job cost data map to your accounting or ERP system, such as Sage, Acumatica, CMiC, Foundation or Viewpoint. Arcoro says most customers are running in 4-6 weeks.

services.name: Paycom
services.tagline: Publicly traded HCM suite with employee-run payroll (Beti) for organizations of 50 to 10,000+ employees
services.pricing_summary: Custom quote; Paycom publishes no prices, and its annual report says pricing is based on employee headcount and the number of applications you use.
services.long_description:
Paycom is a cloud human capital management (HCM) company founded in 1998 and based in Oklahoma City, and it trades on the New York Stock Exchange as PAYC. Its annual report says it targets organizations with 50 to 10,000 or more employees and has about 39,200 clients (about 20,300 when grouped by parent company). Payroll, time and labor, talent acquisition, talent management and HR all run on one database.

Its signature feature is Beti, which Paycom describes as letting employees do their own payroll, reviewing their own paychecks so errors are caught before payroll is final. Other tools include an AI assistant called IWant, automated time-off decisions (GONE), on-demand pay (Everyday), Paycom Pay for checks that clear from a Paycom bank account, labor allocation, certification management, applicant tracking, onboarding, benefits and ACA administration. GL Concierge exports payroll data in custom file layouts for your accounting software.

For a larger trades company, such as a multi-location HVAC, electrical or plumbing firm with office staff and field crews, that single system can replace several separate HR and payroll tools. Paycom does not publish prices; its annual report says pricing depends on headcount and the applications you use, so you get a quote through sales.

The trade-off: it is built for companies with 50 or more employees and sold through sales, so a small shop will find it more system than it needs, and it is a general HCM rather than a construction payroll specialist. Also note that in 2021 the SEC found Paycom had billed some clients for services they already paid for; Paycom returned about $2.8 million to clients and settled without admitting or denying the findings.
services.how_it_works: Paycom is sold through its sales team. You choose the applications you need (payroll, time and labor, talent acquisition, HR, benefits and others) and pricing is set by headcount and applications. Implementation moves your employee data into Paycom's single database. Employees use Beti to check and fix their own paychecks before payroll is final, and managers approve time and time off in the same system. Payroll data exports to your accounting software through custom GL file layouts.

services.name: Miter

services.long_description:
Miter is construction workforce software that puts payroll, HR, expense management and field operations in one product. Co-founder Connor Watumull launched it in 2021, the company (Miter HR, Inc.) lists a San Francisco address, and in May 2025 it announced $38 million in funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Coatue. Miter says it serves more than 2,000 companies and processes more than $8.5 billion in payroll a year.

Payroll is built for construction. Miter says it handles federal, state and local taxes in all 50 states, pays by next-day direct deposit at no extra fee and charges nothing for off-cycle or correction runs. It produces WH-347 and state certified payroll reports, submits directly to state portals in 11 states, exports to LCPtracker and similar systems, and handles Davis-Bacon and state prevailing wage, fringes, union reporting and union reciprocity. Job-coded time from the field flows into payroll, and fully burdened labor costs sync to your ERP for job costing.

Around payroll sit HR tools (HRIS, recruiting, onboarding, benefits, learning, performance), field tools (time tracking, scheduling, production, daily reports, safety) and expense tools (reimbursements, per diems, corporate cards, accounts payable). Its integration page names QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Sage Intacct, Sage 100, Sage 300 CRE, NetSuite, Acumatica, Foundation, Viewpoint, CMiC, Procore and ServiceTitan, among others.

The trade-off: Miter publishes no pricing, so cost is only known after a demo and quote, and it is a younger company (2021) than long-running construction payroll providers. Test the certified payroll reports and ERP sync you depend on during the demo, and compare it with other construction payroll options such as eBacon, Payroll4Construction and Arcoro.
services.how_it_works: After a demo and quote, Miter sets up your employees, jobs, pay rates, prevailing-wage and union rules and your ERP connection. Crews record job-coded time in the field, Miter applies the right rates and fringes, runs payroll (next-day direct deposit at no extra fee), files federal, state and local taxes, generates certified payroll reports or submits them to supported state portals, and syncs labor costs to your accounting system for job costing. HR, expense and field modules run in the same system.

services.long_description:
Wagepoint is online payroll software for small businesses in Canada. It was founded in 2012 by Shrad Rao and Ryan Dineen, private equity firm Providence Strategic Growth took a majority stake in 2020, and its legal entity, Wagepoint Holdings Inc., is based in Calgary, Alberta, with a team that works remotely across Canada. Its pricing page says it currently serves only small businesses in Canada, and it counts more than 30,000 small businesses, accountants and bookkeepers as customers.

The service covers the core of Canadian payroll. Wagepoint says it calculates federal, provincial and territorial withholdings, EI and CPP, submits CRA remittances on your behalf each time you run payroll, generates T4 and T4A slips and files them electronically with the CRA, issues Records of Employment and pays staff by direct deposit. In February 2026 it added Timesheets with automatic overtime and the My Wagepoint mobile app for iOS and Android, and in September 2026 it added Québec payroll (Revenu Québec remittances, RL-1, QPIP and CNESST) at no extra cost.

Pricing is published: Solo costs $20 per month plus $4 per employee or contractor and allows one pay run and one pay group a month, while Unlimited costs $40 per month plus $6 per employee or contractor with unlimited pay runs and pay groups. There are no contracts, support is included, and there is a 14-day free trial. The pricing page does not label the currency. It integrates with QuickBooks Online, Xero and FreshBooks.

The trade-off: Wagepoint only serves Canadian businesses, so a US trades shop needs a US payroll provider. It is payroll-first, without the benefits administration or deeper HR of larger HR platforms, and it has no construction-specific features such as certified or union payroll.
services.how_it_works: You add employees and contractors and set up pay schedules, then run payroll online. Wagepoint calculates withholdings, EI and CPP, pays staff by direct deposit, submits CRA remittances (and Revenu Québec remittances for Québec staff), and produces T4s, T4As, RL-1s and Records of Employment. Hours can come from Timesheets or the My Wagepoint app, and payroll data syncs to QuickBooks Online, Xero or FreshBooks. You pay a monthly base fee plus a per-person fee, with no contract.

service_faqs.q: Is Wagepoint good for US trades businesses?
service_faqs.a: No. Wagepoint's pricing page says it currently serves only small businesses in Canada, so a US trades shop should use a US payroll provider.

service_faqs.q: How much does Wagepoint cost?
service_faqs.a: Solo is $20 per month plus $4 per employee or contractor (one pay run and one pay group a month). Unlimited is $40 per month plus $6 per employee or contractor, with unlimited pay runs and pay groups. There are no contracts and a 14-day free trial; the pricing page does not label the currency.

service_faqs.q: Does Wagepoint remit payroll taxes to the CRA?
service_faqs.a: Yes. Wagepoint says it calculates and submits your CRA remittances each time you run payroll, files T4 and T4A slips electronically, and issues Records of Employment. Since September 2026 it also handles Revenu Québec remittances and RL-1 slips.

service_faqs.q: Does Wagepoint handle construction payroll?
service_faqs.a: It handles standard Canadian payroll and timesheets, but not construction-specific needs such as certified payroll, union fringes or prevailing wage. Contractors with those requirements should use a construction payroll specialist.
